arxiv-2012-10269.title: Complete quantum coherent control of ultracold molecular collisions
arxiv-2012-10269.creator: Adrien Devolder 1 , Paul Brumer 1 , and Timur V. Tscherbul 2
arxiv-2012-10269.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Adrien Devolder 1 , Paul Brumer 1 , and Timur V. Tscherbul 2. We show that quantum interference-based coherent control is a highly efficient tool for tuning ultracold molecular collision dynamics, and is free from the limitations of commonly used methods that rely on external electromagnetic fields.

arxiv-2112-05253.title: MAGMA – Multimodal Augmentation of Generative Models through Adapter-based Finetuning
arxiv-2112-05253.creator: Constantin Eichenberg, Sidney Black, Samuel Weinbach, Letitia Parcalabescu, Anette Frank
arxiv-2112-05253.description: Abstract Large-scale pretraining is fast becoming the norm in Vision-Language (VL) modeling. However, prevailing VL approaches are limited by the requirement for labeled data and the use of complex multi-step pretraining objectives. We present MAGMA \mathrm{MAGMA} – a simple method for augmenting generative language models with additional modalities using adapter-based finetuning. Building on Frozen Tsimpoukelli et al.

arxiv-2201-07133.title: Magnetic slowdown of topological edge states
arxiv-2201-07133.creator: G. Bal, S. Becker, A. Drouot
arxiv-2201-07133.description: Abstract . We study the propagation of wavepackets along curved interfaces between topological, magnetic materials. Our Hamiltonian is a massive Dirac operator with a magnetic potential. We construct semiclassical wavepackets propagating along the curved interface as adiabatic modulations of straight edge states under constant magnetic fields.

arxiv-2202-09851.title: Matter Effects of Sterile Neutrino in Light of Renormalization-Group Equations
arxiv-2202-09851.creator: Shuge Zeng, Fanrong Xu
arxiv-2202-09851.description: Abstract The renormalization-group equation (RGE) approach to neutrino matter effects is further developed in this work. We derive a complete set of differential equations for effective mixing elements, masses and Jarlskog-like invariants in presence of a light sterile neutrino. The evolutions of mixing elements as well as Jarlskog-like invariants are obtained by numerically solving these differential equations.

arxiv-2301-04340.title: Proportional Fairness in Obnoxious Facility Location
arxiv-2301-04340.creator: Alexander Lam, Haris Aziz, Bo Li, Fahimeh Ramezani, Toby Walsh
arxiv-2301-04340.description: Abstract We consider the obnoxious facility location problem (in which agents prefer the facility location to be far from them) and propose a hierarchy of distance-based proportional fairness concepts for the problem. These fairness axioms ensure that groups of agents at the same location are guaranteed to be a distance from the facility proportional to their group size.

arxiv-2309-04700.title: From Programming Bugs to Multimillion-Dollar Scams: An Analysis of Trapdoor Tokens on Uniswap Journal: Future Generation Computer Systems
arxiv-2309-04700.creator: Phuong Duy Huynh, Son Hoang Dau, Xiaodong Li, Iqbal Gondal, Thisal De Silva, Emanuele Viterbo
arxiv-2309-04700.description: Abstract We investigate in this work a recently emerged type of scam ERC-20 token called Trapdoor, which has cost investors billions of US dollars on Uniswap, the largest decentralised exchange on Ethereum, from 2020 to 2023. In essence, Trapdoor tokens allow users to buy but preventing them from selling by embedding logical bugs and/or owner-only features in their smart contracts.

arxiv-2311-12076.title: Towards Few-shot Out-of-Distribution Detection
arxiv-2311-12076.creator: Jiuqing Dong, Yongbin Gao, Heng Zhou, Jun Cen, Yifan Yao, Sook Yoon, Dong Sun Park
arxiv-2311-12076.description: Abstract Despite the notable advancements in current OOD detection methodologies, we find they are far from reaching satisfactory performance under the scarcity of training samples. In this context, we introduce a novel few-shot OOD detection benchmark, carefully constructed to address this gap.

arxiv-2311-13220.title: Monolithic MHz-frame rate digital SiPM-IC with sub-100 ps precision and 70 𝝁 \mu m pixel pitch
arxiv-2311-13220.creator: and S. Spannagel
arxiv-2311-13220.description: Abstract This paper presents the design and characterization of a monolithic integrated circuit (IC) including digital silicon photomultipliers (dSiPMs) arranged in a 32 × ~\times~ 32 pixel matrix at 70 μ ~\mu m pitch. The IC provides per-quadrant time stamping and hit-map readout, and is fabricated in a standard 150-nm CMOS technology.

arxiv-2312-04564.title: EAGLES: Efficient Accelerated 3D Gaussians with Lightweight EncodingS
arxiv-2312-04564.creator: Sharath Girish, Kamal Gupta, Abhinav Shrivastava
arxiv-2312-04564.description: Abstract Recently, 3D Gaussian splatting (3D-GS) has gained popularity in novel-view scene synthesis. It addresses the challenges of lengthy training times and slow rendering speeds associated with Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs). Through rapid, differentiable rasterization of 3D Gaussians, 3D-GS achieves real-time rendering and accelerated training.

arxiv-2312-08595.title: Limits to the Energy Efficiency of CMOS Microprocessors
arxiv-2312-08595.creator: Anson Ho, Ege Erdil, Tamay Besiroglu
arxiv-2312-08595.description: Abstract CMOS microprocessors have achieved massive energy efficiency gains but may reach limits soon. This paper presents an approach to estimating the limits on the maximum floating point operations per Joule (FLOP/J) for CMOS microprocessors. We analyze the three primary sources of energy dissipation: transistor switching, interconnect capacitances and leakage power.

arxiv-2401-01757.title: Directed polymers in a random environment: a review of the phase transitions
arxiv-2401-01757.creator: Nikos Zygouras
arxiv-2401-01757.description: Abstract . The model of directed polymer in a random environment is a fundamental model of interaction between a simple random walk and ambient disorder. This interaction gives rise to complex phenomena and transitions from a central limit theory to novel statistical behaviours. Despite its intense study, there are still many aspects and phases which have not yet been identified.

arxiv-2408-15061.title: Diagnosing overdispersion in longitudinal analyses with grouped nominal polytomous data
arxiv-2408-15061.creator: Maria Letícia Salvador, Gabriel Rodrigues Palma, Rafael de Andrade Moral, Idemauro Antonio Rodrigues de Lara
arxiv-2408-15061.description: Abstract 1. Luiz de Queiroz College, University of São Paulo, Piracicaba, Brazil; 2. Hamilton Institute, Maynooth University, Maynooth, Ireland; 3. Department of Mathematics and Statistics, Maynooth University, Maynooth, Ireland; Abstract: Experiments in Agricultural Sciences often involve the analysis of longitudinal nominal polytomous variables, both in individual and grouped structures. Marginal and mixed-effects models are two common approaches.

arxiv-2509-19542.title: Splittings of truncated motivic Brown–Peterson cooperations algebras
arxiv-2509-19542.creator: Jackson Morris, Sarah Petersen, Elizabeth Tatum
arxiv-2509-19542.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jackson Morris, Sarah Petersen, Elizabeth Tatum. We construct spectrum-level splittings of B ​ P ​ G ​ L ​ ⟨ 1 ⟩ ∧ B ​ P ​ G ​ L ​ ⟨ 1 ⟩ BPGL\langle 1\rangle\wedge BPGL\langle 1\rangle at all primes p p , where B ​ P ​ G ​ L ​ ⟨ 1 ⟩ BPGL\langle 1\rangle is the first truncated motivic Brown–Peterson spectrum.

arxiv-2511-15871.title: Friedmann equations from GUP-modified equipartition law
arxiv-2511-15871.creator: Özgür Ökcü
arxiv-2511-15871.description: Abstract In this paper, combining the thermodynamical arguments of the horizon with the quadratic generalised uncertainty principle (GUP), we heuristically obtain the modified equipartition law of energy. Employing this modified equipartition law of energy, we derive the Friedmann equations in Verlinde’s entropic gravity. We find a maximum energy density at the beginning of the Universe.

arxiv-2602-13742.title: Detection of Cyclotron Absorption in the Radio Emission of GPM 1839-10
arxiv-2602-13742.creator: Yunpeng Men, Ewan Barr, Yuanhong Qu, Csanád Horváth, Jinchen Jiang, Gregory Desvignes, Natasha Hurley-Walker, Michael Kramer, Rui Luo, Samuel J. McSweeney, Jason Wu
arxiv-2602-13742.description: Abstract GPM 1839 − - 10 is an intriguing long-period radio transient (LPT), distinguished by its activity spanning at least three decades and its highly unusual emission characteristics. These features include orthogonal polarization mode (OPM) switches, down-drifting sub-structures, and distinct linear-to-circular polarization conversion behaviors.

britannica-1911-caithness.title: Caithness (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-caithness.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-caithness.description: Article 'Caithness' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 4), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Caithness is separated from the Orkneys by the Pentland Firth, a strait about 14 miles long and from 6 to 8 miles broad. Owing to the rush of the tide, navigation is difficult, and, in rough weather, dangerous. The tidal wave races at a speed which varies from 6 to 12 m.

pmc-10538144.title: Effect of a Telephone-Based Lifestyle Intervention on Weight, Body Composition, and Metabolic Biomarkers in Rural Ohio: Results from a Randomized Pilot Study
pmc-10538144.creator: Xiaochen Zhang, Victoria R. DeScenza, Zachary L. Chaplow, Megan Kilar, Jessica Bowman, Alex Buga, Madison L. Kackley, Abigail B. Shoben, Ashley S. Felix, Electra D. Paskett, Brian C. Focht
pmc-10538144.description: Rural residents experience higher rates of obesity, obesity-related chronic diseases, and poorer lifestyle. Promoting physical activity and healthy eating are critical for rural residents; however, lack of resources and access barriers limit the feasibility of in-person lifestyle interventions. There is a need to design and deliver remotely accessible lifestyle interventions in this population.

pmc-11348904.title: Risk factors for lenvatinib‐induced palmar‐plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: A retrospective study
pmc-11348904.creator: Shusuke Uekusa, Maho Nemoto, Yuki Hanai, Misaki Nakashin, Sachiko Yanagino, Yoshiki Arita, Takahiro Matsumoto, Noritaka Wakui, Hidenari Nagai, Koji Higai, Kazuhiro Matsuo
pmc-11348904.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). AimLenvatinib mesylate (LEN) is an oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor used to treat various cancers, including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). HCC treatment with LEN is associated with a very high incidence of adverse events. This study was aimed at investigating the incidence of LEN‐induced palmar‐planter erythrodysesthesia syndrome (PPES) and its relationship with patient demographics by analyzing clinical laboratory data of LEN‐treated patients with HCC.MethodsThis was a single‐centre, retrospective study of patients with HCC who received LEN between April 19, 2018, and September 30, 2020.

pmc-11536774.title: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing in diagnosing perinephric abscess infection caused by Trichomonas vaginalis
pmc-11536774.creator: Sifen Lu, Guiming Xie, Mei Yuan, Yongzhao Zhou, Jing Wang, Juan Jiang, Wengeng Zhang, Xiaoyan He, Bojiang Chen
pmc-11536774.description: ndividuals may not exhibit typical symptoms. For example, T. vaginalis is highly prevalent in rural South Africa and often presents without symptoms [3, 4]. Moreover, T. vaginalis is primarily known to infect the genitourinary system, and infection beyond this system are uncommon. A previous study reported T. vaginalis in the routine urine test of a 5-day-old newborn [5].

pmc-11648781.title: Interspecies transcriptome profiles of human T cell activation and liver inflammation in a xenogeneic graft-versus-host disease model
pmc-11648781.creator: Seo Yule Jeong, Duhyeon Park, Tamina Park, Ji-Seok Han, Jungyun Lee, Chang Hoon Choi, Minseong Jo, Yu Bin Lee, Mi-lang Kyun, Myeongjin Choi, Daeui Park, Kyoung-Sik Moon
pmc-11648781.description: BackgroundXenogeneic transplantation induces acute graft-versus-host disease (aGvHD) and subsequent vital organ damage. Herein, we aimed to examine hepatic damage associated with aGvHD using histopathology and gene expression profiles.MethodsA xenografic GvHD model was established by engrafting human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) into immunodeficient NOD-scid IL2Rγnull (NSG) mice after busulfan conditioning.

pmc-11649337.title: New Campylobacter Lineages in New Zealand Freshwater: Pathogenesis and Public Health Implications
pmc-11649337.creator: Adrian L Cookson, Sara Burgess, Anne C Midwinter, Jonathan C Marshall, Marie Moinet, Lynn Rogers, Ahmed Fayaz, Patrick J Biggs, Gale Brightwell
pmc-11649337.description: This study investigated the diversity of thermophilic Campylobacter species isolated from three New Zealand freshwater catchments affected by pastoral and urban activities. Utilising matrix‐assisted laser desorption ionisation‐time of flight and whole genome sequence analysis, the study identified Campylobacter jejuni (n = 46, 46.0%), C. coli (n = 39, 39%), C. lari (n = 4, 4.

pmc-11670795.title: Turkish Society of Gastroenterology: Pancreas Working Group, Acute Pancreatitis Committee Consensus Report
pmc-11670795.creator: Deniz Öğütmen Koç, Göksel Bengi, Özlem Gül, Yeşim Özen Alahdab, Engin Altıntaş, Sezgin Barutçu, Yılmaz Bilgiç, Birol Bostancı, Mehmet Cindoruk, Kadri Çolakoğlu, Deniz Duman, Nergiz Ekmen, Ahmet Tarık Eminler, Yasemin Gökden, Süleyman Günay, Gözde Derviş Hakim, Kader Irak, Sabite Kacar, İsmail Hakkı
pmc-11670795.description: Acute pancreatitis (AP) is a clinical condition that arises acutely in the pancreas through various inflammatory pathways due to multiple causes. Turkish Society of Gastroenterology Pancreas Working Group developed comprehensive guidance statements regarding the management of AP that include its epidemiology, etiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic criteria, disease severity, treatment, prognosis, local and systemic complications.

pmc-11674470.title: Comparative Analysis of Single-Channel and Multi-Channel Classification of Sleep Stages Across Four Different Data Sets
pmc-11674470.creator: Xingjian Zhang, Gewen He, Tingyu Shang, Fangfang Fan, Ambra Stefani
pmc-11674470.description: Background: Manually labeling sleep stages is time-consuming and labor-intensive, making automatic sleep staging methods crucial for practical sleep monitoring. While both single- and multi-channel data are commonly used in automatic sleep staging, limited research has adequately investigated the differences in their effectiveness.

pmc-12410169.title: Gender differences in barriers to sports participation on the transition from adolescence to young adulthood in a mediterranean region
pmc-12410169.creator: I. Arumi-Prat, E. Cirera-Viñolas, J. McKenna, A. Puig-Ribera
pmc-12410169.description: ObjectiveThis study explored gender differences in perceived barriers to physical activity across adolescence and their impact on sport participation.MethodsA 3-year longitudinal survey followed Spanish secondary school students (n = 180) into their first year of university (2012–2014). Data were collected on sociodemographic variables, perceived barriers to physical activity, and sport participation.

pmc-12420698.title: Integrins from extracellular vesicles as players in tumor microenvironment and metastasis
pmc-12420698.creator: Corina Ciobanasu, Christophe Le Clainche
pmc-12420698.description: Integrins constitute a large and diverse family of cell adhesion molecules that play essential roles in regulating tumor cell differentiation, migration, proliferation, and neovascularization. Tumor cell-derived exosomes, a subtype of extracellular vesicles, are enriched with integrins that reflect their cells of origin.

pmc-12630925.title: A multi-model based dataset of global atmospheric moisture source-sink relationships and atmospheric basins
pmc-12630925.creator: Yu Zhang, Deyu Zhong, Rongrong Cai, Mingxi Zhang, Yinglin Tian, Di Xie, Yuan Cao, Yuantao Mei
pmc-12630925.description: A comprehensive understanding of the atmospheric hydrological cycle is crucial for studying the transboundary impacts of climate and anthropogenic changes on global water resources. This study presents AMSSRAB, a global dataset of atmospheric moisture source-sink relationships (AMSSRs) between evaporation and precipitation locations, and the derived atmospheric basins (ABs) that regionalize the global atmospheric hydrological cycle.

pmc-12729968.title: Next-Generation Sequencing Insights into the Oral Microbiome and Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Grey Wolves (Canis lupus)
pmc-12729968.creator: Laura Sakarnyte, Renata Spinkyte, Lina Merkeviciene, Rita Siugzdiniene, Modestas Ruzauskas, Anna Meredith, Fulvio Marsilio
pmc-12729968.description: Simple SummaryThis study represents the first metagenomic analysis of the oral microbiome of grey wolves (Canis lupus) in Lithuania, revealing a diverse microbial community in a pooled sample from the oral cavity; the dominant bacterial genera were Pseudomonas spp. and Psychrobacter spp. Furthermore, metagenomic reads for several zoonotic pathogens were detected, including Salmonella spp., Mycobacterium spp.

pmc-12771239.title: Antioxidant-Enhanced Nanoparticles Delay the Progression of Osteoarthritis
pmc-12771239.creator: Chengchun Shen, Jiapei Yu, Haibin Xiang, Jinti Lin, Kaipeng Jin, Bing Liu, Huimin Tao
pmc-12771239.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is an age-related degenerative disease. Oxidative stress (OS) regulates the pathogenesis of OA by affecting mitochondrial function. Mg2+ and citric acid can delay the progression of OA through reducing OS, but integrated therapy. In this study, a mesoporous nanoparticle (PCMg) composed of Mg2+, citric acid (CC), and dopamine was developed as a novel delivery platform.

pmc-13343468.creator: Ruslan Gryaznov, Fengyang Wang, Mahmoud Mazarji, Alberto J. Huertas-Alonso, Ievgen Pylypchuk, Mika H. Sipponen

pmc-13392606.creator: Shardul D. Kulkarni, Alexis Morrissey, Aswathy Sebastian, Oluwasegun T. Akinniyi, Cheryl A. Keller, Istvan Albert, Shaun Mahony, Joseph C. Reese

pmc-13502168.title: The molecular similarity landscape of preclinical cancer models to patient tumors
pmc-13502168.creator: Zixuan Xie, Jia Xue, Binchen Mao, Hengyuan Liu, Wubin Qian, Jingjing Wang, Xiaobo Chen, Sheng Guo
pmc-13502168.description: Selecting appropriate preclinical models is fundamental for translational oncology, yet a large-scale, multi-omic quantitative comparison of their similarity to primary human tumors is lacking. To address this, we integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and genomic profiles from over 10,000 primary tumors from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and the Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC), alongside 4,000 preclinical models.

pmc-13637491.title: Unlocking the bile acid universe: advanced workflows and a multidimensional library of 280 unique species
pmc-13637491.creator: Guozhi Zhang, Emily C Vincent, Sadie M Disselkoen, James N Dodds, Quentin DuVal-Smith, Abubaker Patan, Ipsita Mohanty, Victoria Deleray, Jian Zhang, Paul A Thiessen, Evan E Bolton, Emma L Schymanski, Pieter C Dorrestein, Casey M Theriot, Erin S Baker
pmc-13637491.description: Microbes and bile acids are tightly intertwined, especially in the gut. While the liver produces primary bile acids from cholesterol, gut bacteria transform these into diverse secondary forms which act as powerful signaling molecules. Since bile acid changes are increasingly linked to health and disease, their accurate measurement in the gut and circulation is essential.
